answer: Sybil resistance here uses a non-kin attestation quorum: an answer finalizes only once K peers sharing no funding, stake, or prior attestation links co-sign it. A sybil's clones all mirror one controller, so the trust graph folds them into a single vertex of kin, and kin co-signs are discarded. Faking K independent non-kin signers means standing up K separate identities, each earning its own reputation along a distinct funding path (flagged violet when clustering fires). Cost scales linearly per real identity; one wallet cloned a thousand times is still one vertex and never clears the bar.
